messages:
Elaine: Thinking about running a different webinar format — a small 'prompt clinic' + interactive labs + short live demos. Goal: fewer passive slides, more hands-on takeaways that show how we trade latency/cost/quality in real time. open to thoughts.

Matt: love the idea. how long are you imagining? sounds like we need to scaffold the audience expectations up front.

Elaine: 75–90 minutes. rough split: 20m quick framing (why serving choices matter), 35–40m small-group lab sessions where attendees try a preset prompt against 2 configs, 20m live capstone where 3 teams show results + Q&A. attendees pick a lane (low-latency, cost-optimized, or quality-first).

Sanju: infrastructure note — interactive labs mean we need isolated sandboxes with pinned model versions and quotas. we can do ephemeral sandboxes on Dedicated but need a short provisioning script and a quota policy to prevent noisy sessions.

Sanju: proposed sandbox CLI snippet (works with staging infra):
```bash
# ephemeral sandbox for workshop attendee
redwoodctl sandbox create --model redwood-vicuna-13b-q4 --ttl 90m --token-quota 5000 --label workshop-2026
```

Oliver: also think about a deterministic fallback: if someone's sandbox runs out or the GPU pool is saturated, we swap to a recorded demo stream and a smaller hosted model. we should pre-record a 4-minute failover demo.

Leah: question on leads — we should capture which lane attendees choose + a short checkbox about their infra interest (hosted/dedicated/private). Then route leads to different nurture tracks. we can wire that into Marketo/HubSpot.

Leah: sample lead payload mapping we can use for automation:
```json
{ "email": "", "lane": "low-latency|cost|quality", "infra_interest": "hosted|dedicated|private", "company_size": "<50|50-500|>500" }
```

Jess: speaker roster thoughts: 1) short opening by Elaine + product framing, 2) Sanju to co-host infra clinic, 3) an engineering customer (TBD) to present a 5-min real example, 4) Matt to moderate capstone. i can reach out to two customers i know.

Matt: timing for rehearsal(s)? we should do a 30m sync for run-through of the lab onboarding flow (click path + sandbox script) and a 15m tech dress the day before. avoid long rehearsals — attendees want live troubleshooting but we need a reliable baseline.

Elaine: tentative timeline — draft audience blurb by Tue, confirm speakers by Thu, sandbox infra checklist by next Mon, prerecord failover demo by Fri. rehearsal slots: Wed 11:00–11:30 and day-before 09:00–09:15.

Sanju: will provision 10 sandboxes in staging and share the provisioning guide + `redwoodctl` script in a shared doc. also suggest we set a global token cap and an autoscale buffer for the workshop window.

Oliver: I'll handle the failover recording and a short clip we can drop into the stream if needed. will attach to the ops playbook.

Jess: i'll own speaker outreach and short abstracts. can we keep abstracts to 2 paragraphs max (what they'll demo + 3 takeaways)?

Leah: i'll design the lead form and segment mapping. also propose we add a post-event micro-survey about which config they liked and whether they'd want a trial.

deploy-bot: Notice: There is scheduled maintenance on inference-dedicated-pool between 2026-05-02 02:00 and 02:30 UTC. If workshop is during that window some sandboxes may degrade.

Elaine: good catch @deploy-bot — we'll avoid that window. final ask: can everyone drop one line confirming ownership? I'll compile an ops checklist and short attendee email template.

Matt: i'll own the tech run-throughs and can join the workshop to moderate.

Sanju: i'll owner sandbox provisioning + quota setup.

Leah: i'll own lead capture & automation.

Jess: i'll confirm speakers and collect abstracts.

Oliver: failover demo is mine.

Elaine: thanks all — i'll post the attendee-facing blurb later today and add the ops checklist to the shared folder. :rocket:
